S11 row_count records full source-file data rows, excluding the header; it is not necessarily the number of rows plotted in that panel. Semicolon-separated counts correspond to semicolon-separated filenames.
Scientific values retain their original numerical precision. Cell formatting affects display only.
NA means unavailable, undefined or not applicable. Missing results are distinct from zero; blank applicability fields contain no reported value.
Absent channels have zero restart count and mass; their cosine, localization contrast and top-stage call are undefined.
S5 includes channel summaries at all four thresholds. Six stage-specific cosine columns are available at 200 and 500 genes; these columns remain NA at 50 and 100 genes.
Each nonempty restart channel is normalized separately. Native absolute-weight shares describe input composition, not final propagated mass proportions.
EPr = early prenatal; MPr = mid prenatal; LPr = late prenatal; EPost = early postnatal; C/A = childhood–adolescence; Adult = adulthood.
Mean cosine across early/mid/late prenatal profiles minus mean cosine across early postnatal/childhood–adolescence/adulthood. Positive values indicate greater prenatal similarity.

Common profile mean/variance quintile matching without replacement for all six comparisons; B=1,000; seed=202609301; plus-one two-sided empirical P and BH-FDR across six tests. Null quantiles describe background variation.
Frequency among the 1,000 random modules of the observed top stage. This is descriptive and is distinct from the two-sided contrast P value and FDR.
Descriptive late-prenatal profile with positive contrast, but lower prenatal contrast than its matched-random background.
The downregulated module has a postnatal/adult reference profile relative to matched gene sets. Reference stage describes expression context, not age of disease onset.
Near-balanced magnitude contrast with distinct positive- and negative-channel profiles; the individual channel patterns are descriptive.
Fraction of simulation replicates for which the highest-ranked developmental state is in the true-state set. Source variable: alignment_hit_top1.
Sum of normalized affinity assigned to the true developmental states. Reported only when the method has a defined affinity readout.
Proportion of true target genes among the 50 highest-ranked genes in one simulation replicate; tables report replicate means. It is a ranking metric, not a P value.
AUROC = area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. AUPRC uses average precision for gene ranking.
high_signal and challenging_signal identify the two simulation designs. Each has six conditions and 200 replicates per condition. ALL_CONDITIONS identifies a pooled summary.
The designs use different condition sets. S7b retains the original condition identifiers and corresponding results.

Simulation identifiers in S7–S7c correspond to the display labels in Fig. 5 and Fig. S2. Archived identifiers and source filenames retain their original spelling; current panel labels use lowercase letters.

These labels denote the simulation-specific signature/embedding composite scorers defined in Methods. The graph-labelled scorer adds community smoothing; they are not evaluations of a separate published optimal-transport solver.
Simulation-only composite of developmental similarity, smoothing and prior/invariance terms; distinct from the dual-head gene-first PPR implementation.
S7c BH-FDR values refer to condition-specific comparator tests within each design and metric. Pooled ALL_CONDITIONS rows are not assigned an FDR in this family; undefined tests remain NA.
Two-sided regression t-test P values; BH-FDR across 36 models. Standardized beta is in cohort-specific score SD units. 95% Student-t intervals use df_resid=18 (GSE64018) or 47 (GSE102741).
delta_standardized_beta_signed_minus_native is the signed-PPR minus native standardized beta for the same cohort, module and threshold. It may repeat across rows and is not a test of the difference.
S1 and S8 counts describe analyzed individuals or samples, rather than complete source collections. Some diagnostic comparisons share controls, and gene-selection thresholds are nested.
S9 marker-adjustment minima and maxima are cohort ranges, not confidence intervals. NNLS adjustment uses the reported adjusted/original beta ratio.
S9 Top 200/Top 500 labels specify native gene-set thresholds. Donors: PsychENCODE 60; Velmeshev microglia 29 and each other displayed cell type 31 at both thresholds.
S10 concerns native modules. Positive-test counts include shared controls and nested thresholds; they are not independent replication counts. The MDD result applies to the available GSE53987 subset.
Effects and direction counts are descriptive. No pooled significance test was applied because comparisons share controls and nested gene sets. MDD model FDR is within disease.
S12 reports the analysis and figure-generation versions recorded with the study. Original execution-session versions for Python and R were not separately documented.
Resource and citation URLs are supplied in S1. An unavailable instrument, donor count or identifier remains NA or explicitly unspecified rather than inferred from the full source resource.

ASD, autism spectrum disorder; NTM, NeuroTRACE-derived transcriptomic module; PPR, personalized PageRank; BH, Benjamini–Hochberg; FDR, false discovery rate; CI, confidence interval; SD, standard deviation; SE, standard error; PC, principal component; NNLS, non-negative least squares.
RIN, RNA integrity number; PMI, postmortem interval; SCZ, schizophrenia; BD, bipolar disorder; MDD, major depressive disorder; OPC, oligodendrocyte precursor cell.
